then.text: Our Silk Square suits you. Mind the tart crumbs.
Charles Roe opened the first big silk mill here in 1743. By Victorian times Macclesfield was one of the great silk towns of England.
So. When did the Jacquard looms at Paradise Mill stop working?
1981! Within living memory. Silk was woven on those handlooms in Macclesfield into the age of the home computer, which, if you think about it, is just a Jacquard loom that sulks.
Here. A silk square from our own loom, and a Bakewell tart from the café, because history is hungry work.
There are plaques like that all over the isles, you know. Read them as you go. Your Gazetteer will thank you, and so will I.

else.text: Not quite. Pop back down to the mill and read the plaque again. It's round and blue. You can't miss it, though people do.
Did the weaver like the card? Good. Now, did you read the blue plaque on the front of Paradise Mill? Go and have a look. There'll be a question. I'm like that.
The weaver at Paradise Mill is waiting on that card. Down past the market, over the river. Unfolded, please.
Welcome to the Silk Museum. Macclesfield made silk for centuries, and this is the town's memory of it.
Charles Roe opened the first big silk mill here in 1743. By Victorian times Macclesfield was one of the great silk towns of England.
One cocoon is a single thread, up to about a kilometre long. A silkworm is a very small, very patient knitter.
Silk was 'thrown' here. That does not mean tossed about. Throwing is twisting the raw threads together into yarn.
You've got the look of somebody with working legs. Could you run an errand for a museum? It's not glamorous. Museums rarely are.
This is a Jacquard card: a weaving pattern, punched as holes in stiff card. A loom reads it row by row. The weaver at Paradise Mill is expecting it.
Paradise Mill is down past the market and over the river. Don't fold it. Folding is how you end up with a tie that says HELP.

macc_silkmuseum_1.text: I came for the silk ties and stayed for the Jacquard cards. Holes in card, pattern in cloth.
Computers borrowed that trick later. Macclesfield got there first, with more style.
